subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls (CloudScale)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls (CloudScale)

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the open items / next steps.

Pain points & goals we heard
- Need per-customer rate limits (QPS) and monthly token quotas to prevent noisy tenants from impacting others.
- Want tier-based routing (free, standard, enterprise) so higher-paying customers hit larger models / dedicated pools.
- Need per-tenant usage and cost allocation reporting (token-level attribution) for billing back to customers.
- Strong requirement to isolate customer data/contexts and have per-tenant audit logs for compliance (SOC 2).

Current stack
- SaaS on GCP behind API Gateway; you currently use per-tenant API keys and a custom API rate limiter.
- No centralized model routing today; single model endpoint shared across tenants.

Success criteria (what would make this a win)
- Enforce configurable per-tenant QPS and monthly token quotas with alerts on breach.
- Policy-based routing: route tenants by tier to specific model variants or dedicated pools.
- Visibility: per-tenant metrics in dashboard + raw usage export for billing.
- Latency SLOs maintained for enterprise tier (<200ms p95) and documented fallback behavior.

Open questions / constraints
- Do you have hard regulatory constraints beyond SOC 2 (e.g., HIPAA)?
- How many tenants do you expect in year 1 / year 2? (ballpark)
- Any blacklisted countries or region-based routing needs?

Next steps
1) I'll send a short checklist and our feature mapping (attached).
2) Schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive with Marissa (solutions engineer) to walk routing/policy config and demo the tenant dashboard — proposed times below.
3) We'll follow with a bill-of-materials + indicative pricing for enterprise vs standard tier routing options.

Proposed times for deep-dive (PST): Wed 08/05 10:00-10:45 or Thu 08/06 14:00-14:45. Let us know what works.

Attachments: Prod-MultiTenancy-Controls-Checklist.pdf

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls (CloudScale)

Thanks Ben — this is helpful.

Couple clarifications:
- We expect ~1,800 tenants Y1 and ~10k Y2 (varying sizes).
- We currently enforce API key-based rate limiting at the gateway but it is coarse and hard to manage per-tenant tiers.
- SOC 2 is required; HIPAA is not in scope now but possible later.
- For enterprise customers we'd prefer options: (A) dedicated GPU pools, or (B) priority routing to larger shared pools — cost and SLA tradeoffs.

One ask: can you include a short note on how billing attribution would work? We need token-level export to our billing system (we use Zuora) and ideally a daily CSV export per tenant.

Wed 08/05 10:00 PST works for Marissa's deep-dive.

Thanks,
Aisha

Aisha — thanks for the quick answers, and great to lock Wed 08/05 10:00 PST for the deep-dive.

On your questions:
- Scale: 1.8k -> 10k tenants is well within what our routing/policy layer supports; we'll discuss sharding and KV cache implications in the deep-dive.
- Billing attribution: Redwood can emit per-request token attribution and a daily usage export (CSV) per tenant. We can also push to an S3 bucket or a secure GCS path for your Zuora ingestion. I'll include a sample export schema in the Drive link.
- Enterprise routing options: both A (dedicated GPU pools) and B (priority routing to larger shared pools) are supported. Tradeoffs we'll cover: cost predictability vs isolation and stricter latency SLOs.

I've attached the tenant mapping template you requested (CloudScale-tenant-mapping.xlsx) and a short FAQ.

Related links:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/CLDS-2026-081
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B-example

Marissa — can you prepare a short demo focused on:
- policy UI for QPS/quotas
- tier-based routing rules
- per-tenant metrics and daily export
- example of routing to dedicated pool vs model variant

Lauren — looping you in for commercial questions on the pricing options.

Thanks,
Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls (CloudScale)

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the context — excited to dig in on Wed.

Technical notes ahead of the call:
- Integration: we'll ask you to send tenant_id in the request header (x-cloudscale-tenant-id) so we can attribute cache/KV and metrics correctly.
- Routing policies: we support rule-based routing (by tenant_id, tag, or tier) and fallback chains (e.g., if dedicated pool unavailable, route to priority shared pool + notify).
- Rate limits & quotas: per-tenant QPS limits at the edge and token quotas enforced at the service level with configurable soft/hard thresholds and alerting.
- Billing export: daily CSV with columns (date, tenant_id, tokens_prompt, tokens_completion, total_tokens, model, route, cost_estimate). We'll provide a sample file during the demo.
- Cache strategy: suggest per-tenant KV cache for heavy enterprise tenants to reduce token costs and latency; we'll run a quick cost model on the call.

I will demo a short flow that configures a tier-based route and run a test tenant through it.

See you Wed 08/05 10:00 PST. Link will be sent shortly.

Cheers,
Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
